messages:
elaine: quick q about 429 contract for per-route quotas — want to confirm intended client behavior and backwards compatibility. can 429 responses include route-specific fields in the body (bucket id, remaining, reset) or should that be header-only?

rajesh: i'd prefer headers for quick client checks, body for extra debugging. headers are cheap to parse.

tom_w: +1 headers for runtime decisions. if we add body fields we should make them optional so older clients ignore them.

elaine: agreed. concrete example i was proposing: 3 headers: `X-RateLimit-Bucket`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `Retry-After`. body could include `\{"bucket\": \"route:generate:prod\", \"detail\": \"burst exhausted\", \"reset_at\": 1680000000\}` — is that acceptable?

rajesh: header names look good. note: `Retry-After` must stay numeric seconds for backcompat. if we add `X-RateLimit-Reset` (unix ts) that could be helpful too.

pm-lex: from product POV we want clients to be able to show a user-facing message with an ETA. so `X-RateLimit-Reset` unix ts + optional body `message` is nice. but don't break old SDKs.

elaine: ok so contract proposal:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:generate:prod
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1977654921  # unix ts when bucket available
Retry-After: 60
Content-Type: application/json

{ "bucket": "route:generate:prod", "message": "burst capacity reached; retry after 60s", "suggested_fallback": "gpt-small" }
```
body fields optional. headers are canonical for client flow control.

tom_w: small nit: `X-RateLimit-Remaining` should be integer >=0. when remaining=0 we should include a `X-RateLimit-Limit` header too so clients can show limit.

rajesh: +1 include `X-RateLimit-Limit`. also clarify semantics for "per-route" vs global bucket: sometimes multiple routes share same bucket id for global quota. the bucket id string should be opaque. clients must not infer structure from it.

elaine: good point — will document that bucket ids are opaque. question: burst handling — if request exceeds short-term burst but global quota still positive, do we return 429 or queue? runtime currently: if no queued capacity, immediate 429. should we try a best-effort fallback to a lower-cost model automatically for hosted tier?

pm-lex: product likes graceful degrade, but only if we can guarantee same safety/semantics. prefer explicit opt-in per-customer. we can't silently swap models for privacy-sensitive customers.

rajesh: implementable as routing policy: if route config has `fallback_model=gpt-small` and customer allows model fallback, then runtime can route to fallback; otherwise return 429 with headers. logging must include `fallback_taken: true` in observability.

elaine: perfect. one more: backward compat — if we add `X-RateLimit-Reset` header, older clients that only read `Retry-After` will still behave. new clients should prefer `X-RateLimit-Reset` for precise ETA. we'll add guidance: prefer `X-RateLimit-Reset` (unix ts), fallback to `Retry-After` (seconds).

tom_w: for SDKs, add helper that normalizes to a single `retryAt` timestamp. i'll add a PR to node/python SDKs. pinging @tom_w for review when i draft contract doc. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-check: rate-limit headers change will be feature-flagged behind `rl_headers_v2` for 2 weeks. will log mismatches to `eng-platform-rate` channel.

elaine: thanks all — i'll draft the spec now with these points (headers canonical, optional body extra, opaque bucket ids, include Limit/Remaining/Reset, Retry-After numeric for backcompat, optional per-customer fallback routing). tagging @rajesh for routing behavior details and @pm-lex for product acceptance.

rajesh: will add a small diagram to show decision flow (fallback allowed? -> route to fallback else 429).

pm-lex: fine with this approach. please add note about telemetry + billing impact when fallback models used.

elaine: noted, will include. thanks everyone, i'll post the spec link shortly. :rocket:
